big_idea: BIG amounts use BILLS. $25 has many combinations.
learning_intention: We are learning to mix bills and coins to make amounts up to $50.
student_learning_goal: I can mix bills and coins to make amounts up to $50.
success_criteria: I can MAKE $25 with bills + coins.
I can FIND 3 ways for an amount.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Tappy + Lou — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Coin + Bill Cards (1 set per pair)

minds_on.hook: Tappy: BIG amounts use BILLS. $25 has many ways! Tappy opens: 'BILLS for tens, COINS for cents!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Tappy and Lou puppets. 'Money friends — yesterday was $1. Today: $25 — bigger amount, more ways!'

Demo 3 ways for $25:
- WAY 1: 1 TWENTY + 1 FIVER (20 + 5 = $25).
- WAY 2: 2 TENS + 1 FIVER (10 + 10 + 5 = $25).
- WAY 3: 1 TWENTY + 5 LOONIES (20 + 5 = $25).

Class verifies each total.

'Tappy says — bills + coins MIX. Same amount, MANY combos.'

Demo 4th way. '12 toonies + 1 loonie = $24 + $1 = $25!'

Now show wrong combo. '1 ten + 1 fiver + 1 fiver = $20. NOT $25!'

'Tappy says — verify the TOTAL!'

Now each pair gets Bill + Coin Cards + Record Strip. Target: $35 (NEW for them). Find 3 ways.

'Tappy says — bills FIRST, then coins to fill in!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Bill + Coin Cards. Target: $35. Find 3 ways.
Stretch: $35 using only TENS and LOONIES.
Help by starting with biggest bill first.

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between bill stations. NO-MATERIALS PATH: children use FINGERS as bills (whole hand = $20 bill, one finger = $5, thumb = $10). Body becomes the wallet.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: makes $35; verifies; records; mixes bills and coins; finds 3.

discussion_prompts: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their $35 combos. Which used FEWER pieces? Which started with the BIGGEST bill? Cite NCTM equivalent-representation principle.
consolidation.exit_routine: Tappy's bills-and-coins refrain — 'BILLS for tens, COINS for cents — together they MAKE the AMOUNT!' Class chants. Each child writes one $35 combo with mixed bill+coin pieces.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child uses 35 LOONIES for $35 — repairing the all-coins trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On bills + coins composition (e.g., $35 = $20 + $10 + $5 OR $25 + $10 + 4 quarters OR many alternatives), the trap is single-strategy fixation — child finds ONE combo and stops. NCTM Principles to Actions on equivalent representations and Carpenter & Moser CGI part-whole composition place flexibility as the gateway to multi-step money fluency.

Yesterday Lou built $1 many ways. Today extends to bills + mixed denominations. Lesson 4 hundreds; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Tappy asks — that's a LOT of coins. What about a BILL?'

Probe. '$20 bill = 20 loonies in 1 piece. Faster!'

Generalise. 'Tappy says — for big amounts, USE BILLS first, coins to fill.'

If still all coins: 'Try the $20 bill. + $10 + $5 = $35. Just 3 pieces!'
common_misconceptions: Coins always = simpler. (Repair: bills for big amounts.)
Bills only for $50+. (Repair: any big amount.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child finds $35 with one $20 + one $10 + one $5 and stops: hide the $20; force a non-$20 route.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can't compose $35 at all: drop to round values ($30, $40); add $5 increments.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child uses bills only OR coins only: require MIXED — at least one bill AND at least one coin per combo.

parts_outline.task: Show 3 ways to make $25 (mix bills + coins).
For 3 combos, mark TRUE if total = $35.
What's the FEWEST bills + coins to make $50?
